policy: supp.* 骨架層(D17)。西式營養補充劑產品——不是 herb.* 飲片/顆粒,不是 drug.* 處方藥。每個帶主張的欄位掛來源(NIH ODS > Examine.com > Natural Medicines > 官方單張/藥典 > 綜述論文,docs/SUPP_CARD_TEMPLATE.md §2);查不到就留空,不填樣板句。interaction_flags 是審閱旗標,不是斷言;CR-009 supp→drugclass 關係種子仍在 staging,尚未審閱前不落 related_drugclass_review_flags。herb/supp 同源物質分開建卡,經 related_herb_id 單側連結(D13)。

interaction_focus_vocabulary.note: interaction_focus 的三個審閱類別與五個狀態值(CR-006 triage 正規化)。狀態不是斷言,是「這一類藥要不要人工覆核」的旗標;除 no_specific_flag_in_source 外一律需要覆核。原始研究包字串保留在 staged_label,正規化可回溯。

statuses.known_concern: Primary source names a specific concern with this drug class.
statuses.possible_concern: Plausible, theoretical, case-level, or product-dependent signal; not established.
statuses.component_dependent: Multi-ingredient product — review each ingredient and dose separately.
statuses.no_specific_flag_in_source: Primary source was reviewed and carries no class-specific flag. NOT equivalent to 'no interaction'.
statuses.insufficient_data: Evidence insufficient. Must not be converted to 'no interaction'.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adults: DRI 600–800 IU/day (15–20 mcg); common supplement products often provide ~1,000–2,000 IU/day; adult UL 4,000 IU/day unless medically supervised.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Excess intake can cause hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria.
Thiazide diuretics can increase hypercalcemia risk; corticosteroids and some weight-loss/cholesterol drugs can alter vitamin D status/absorption.
No specific anticoagulant, immunosuppressant, or thyroid-drug interaction is a defining D3 interaction, but medication review remains appropriate.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Thiazide diuretics can raise hypercalcemia risk; other drugs affecting vitamin D or calcium handling warrant review.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Established nutrient for calcium/bone metabolism; supplementation benefit is strongest for preventing/treating deficiency rather than as a universal disease treatment.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No standardized formula. Usually provides multiple B vitamins from around Daily Value levels to high multiples; assess each component separately, especially B6, niacin, folic acid, and B12.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Safety depends on individual component doses; high-dose B6 can cause neuropathy and niacin can cause flushing/hepatotoxicity at pharmacologic doses.
Folic acid can mask hematologic signs of B12 deficiency.
Review interactions component-by-component; no single class-wide anticoagulant/immunosuppressant/thyroid interaction rule.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Review B6, niacin, folate and B12 amounts separately; a blend does not carry one class-wide interaction conclusion.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Useful when one or more B-vitamin needs are not met, but a B-complex is not one standardized intervention and evidence cannot be generalized across formulations.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA 2.4 mcg/day; oral supplements commonly contain much higher amounts (e.g. 25–1,000+ mcg) because absorption is limited and dose-dependent.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Generally low toxicity; no established UL.
Metformin and acid-suppressing drugs can reduce B12 status over time.
No characteristic anticoagulant/immunosuppressant/thyroid-drug interaction.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Metformin and acid-suppressing drugs can contribute to low B12 status over time.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Strong evidence for correcting B12 deficiency; benefit in people with adequate status for nonspecific energy/cognition claims is not established.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adults DFE RDA 400 mcg/day; pregnancy 600 mcg DFE/day. Common supplements often provide 400–800 mcg folic acid or equivalent; adult UL for folic acid from supplements/fortified foods is 1,000 mcg/day.

key_safety_notes.note_en: High folic acid intake can mask hematologic signs of vitamin B12 deficiency.
Interacts with some antifolate drugs and antiseizure medicines; medication-specific review required.
No general anticoagulant or thyroid-drug warning.

immunosuppressant.note_en: Antifolate drugs — a group that overlaps with agents used as immunosuppressants — are the relevant interaction.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Antifolate and some antiseizure medicines are more relevant here than the three focus classes; high folic acid intake can mask hematologic signs of B12 deficiency.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Established role in one-carbon metabolism and prevention of neural tube defects when adequate folic acid is taken per public-health guidance around conception.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Common clinical-study/supplement range ~100–300 mg/day; higher doses have been studied for specific conditions. No U.S. RDA.

key_safety_notes.note_en: May interact with warfarin and potentially reduce anticoagulant effect; monitor if combined.
May interact with insulin/diabetes treatment.
Compatibility with some cancer treatments is uncertain; coordinate with oncology team.

anticoagulant.note_en: May reduce warfarin effect; monitor anticoagulation clinically if combined.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: May also interact with insulin and diabetes treatment; compatibility with some cancer treatments is uncertain and should be coordinated with the oncology team.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Evidence is condition-specific and mixed; NCCIH does not support broad disease-treatment claims, though limited signals exist in selected cardiovascular/migraine contexts.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Common research dosing ~120–240 mg/day standardized extract, divided or once/twice daily; product standardization matters.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Potential bleeding risk/interaction concern with anticoagulant or antiplatelet drugs; perioperative review warranted.
Seeds are toxic when raw/roasted in quantity; supplement data mainly concern leaf extract.
No established thyroid-drug benefit; medication review required.

anticoagulant.note_en: Bleeding interaction concern with anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy; perioperative review warranted.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Supplement interaction data concern standardized leaf extract; raw or roasted seeds eaten in quantity are a separate toxic exposure.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: NCCIH reports no conclusive evidence that ginkgo is helpful for any health condition; dementia prevention and tinnitus benefit have not been demonstrated.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Research products vary widely, commonly hundreds of mg to ~1–2 g/day curcuminoids/turmeric extracts; formulations are not dose-equivalent because bioavailability differs.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Highly bioavailable formulations have been associated with liver injury; stop and evaluate if jaundice/dark urine or marked systemic symptoms occur.
Potential antiplatelet/bleeding interaction is plausible; use caution with anticoagulants/antiplatelets.
Piperine-containing products can alter drug exposure; interaction review is important.

anticoagulant.note_en: Antiplatelet and bleeding concern is plausible rather than established; use caution with anticoagulants and antiplatelets.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Piperine-containing and enhanced-bioavailability products can alter drug exposure, so interaction review must name the specific formulation.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: NCCIH considers evidence insufficient for definitive health-purpose conclusions; osteoarthritis results are promising but not definitive.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Common eye-health formulations/studies often use lutein 10 mg/day with zeaxanthin 2 mg/day; no RDA established.

dose_source.name: NIH National Eye Institute — AREDS2 results (lutein/zeaxanthin 10 mg/2 mg)
dose_source.note: AREDS2 formula dose; replaces dead ODS directory link (2026-08-11 fix, prior link did not support the claim)

key_safety_notes.note_en: Generally well tolerated in studied doses; high carotenoid intake can cause benign skin discoloration.
No defining anticoagulant/immunosuppressant/thyroid-drug interaction established.
Combination products may introduce other interaction risks.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Downgraded from the staging matrix's 'no specific flag' to insufficient data: NIH ODS has no lutein ingredient fact sheet — the cited ODS page is a directory index that routes to an external entry — so no primary source was actually reviewed for these three classes. Combination eye-health products may also introduce interactions from their other ingredients.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Lutein/zeaxanthin are retinal carotenoids; evidence is strongest in specific ophthalmic contexts and combination formulations rather than as a general-purpose supplement.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No standard formulation or dose; many products provide nutrients near Daily Values, while high-potency products may greatly exceed them.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Interaction and toxicity profile depends on ingredients and dose; duplicate intake with other supplements is a major issue.
Vitamin K-containing products can affect warfarin management.
Minerals such as calcium/iron can interfere with levothyroxine absorption if taken too close together.

anticoagulant.note_en: Vitamin K-containing products can affect warfarin management.

thyroid.note_en: Calcium and iron can impair levothyroxine absorption when taken too close together.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: The interaction profile follows the specific ingredient list and doses; duplicate intake alongside single-ingredient supplements is the major practical issue.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: MVMs can help fill nutrient gaps, but compositions vary widely and broad prevention benefits are not uniform across outcomes.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA generally 1,000–1,200 mg/day total intake depending on age/sex. Supplemental doses are often 500–600 mg per dose; total intake should account for diet. Adult UL commonly 2,000–2,500 mg/day depending on age.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Higher supplemental intake can increase kidney-stone risk in some people.
Calcium can reduce absorption of levothyroxine; separate administration per medication guidance.
Also interacts with some antibiotics and bisphosphonates; no defining anticoagulant interaction.

thyroid.note_en: Calcium reduces levothyroxine absorption; separate administration per medication guidance.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Also interacts with some antibiotics and with bisphosphonates; higher supplemental intake can raise kidney-stone risk in some people.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Essential for bone and neuromuscular physiology; supplementation is most rational when dietary intake is inadequate or specific clinical indications exist.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA from all sources roughly 310–420 mg/day by age/sex. Supplemental products often provide ~100–350 mg elemental magnesium/day; U.S. UL for supplemental magnesium is 350 mg/day, excluding food magnesium.

key_safety_notes.note_en: High supplemental doses commonly cause diarrhea; extreme doses can cause serious toxicity, especially with renal impairment.
Can reduce absorption of some antibiotics and bisphosphonates; separate dosing.
No defining anticoagulant or thyroid interaction, but product timing with medications should be reviewed.

thyroid.note_en: Timing against thyroid medication should be checked against the exact product and medication guidance.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: The strongest established timing interactions are with selected antibiotics and bisphosphonates; extreme doses can cause serious toxicity in renal impairment.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Essential mineral with established deficiency indications; evidence for symptom-specific supplementation varies by condition and baseline status.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA 8 mg/day women and 11 mg/day men; common supplements often 10–30 mg/day. Adult UL 40 mg/day.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Chronic high doses can cause copper deficiency and neurologic/hematologic problems.
Interacts with quinolone/tetracycline antibiotics and penicillamine; separate dosing.
No defining anticoagulant or thyroid-drug interaction.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Key interactions are with quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics and with penicillamine; separate dosing. Chronic high doses can cause copper deficiency.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Established nutrient with clear deficiency treatment value. Benefit beyond correcting inadequate zinc status is indication-specific.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Well-studied regimen: loading ~20 g/day divided for 5–7 days, then maintenance ~3–5 g/day; loading is optional.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Typical doses are generally well tolerated in healthy adults; weight gain from water retention and GI effects can occur.
People with kidney disease or complex medical conditions should use clinician guidance.
No characteristic anticoagulant/immunosuppressant/thyroid-drug interaction established.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Kidney disease and complex medical context are more relevant to review than these three drug classes.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: One of the best-supported sports supplements for repeated high-intensity exercise, strength and power; little value for endurance performance.

records.name_zh: NAD+（菸醯胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸）
common_forms_en: IV/IM products marketed outside standard supplement evidence base

key_safety_notes.note_en: Long-term safety and clinically meaningful oral bioavailability are uncertain.
Interaction data with anticoagulants, immunosuppressants, and thyroid drugs are insufficient rather than proven absent.
Parenteral NAD+ should not be treated as equivalent to ordinary dietary-supplement use.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Sparse interaction evidence must not be read as absence of interaction; parenteral NAD+ products are not equivalent to ordinary dietary-supplement use.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Human evidence for direct NAD+ supplementation is limited; avoid extrapolating benefits observed with NR/NMN or preclinical NAD biology to direct NAD+ products.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Human trials commonly study ~100–1,000 mg/day; one randomized trial found 100–1,000 mg/day well tolerated over 8 weeks. No RDA established.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Short-term human safety is reasonably characterized at studied doses, but long-term clinical outcome data remain limited.
Interaction data with anticoagulants/immunosuppressants/thyroid drugs are insufficient.
Do not infer anti-aging or disease-treatment benefit from NAD+ biomarker increases alone.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Short-term human safety at studied doses does not establish broad drug-interaction absence.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: NR can raise NAD-related biomarkers in humans, but clinically meaningful benefits for aging or disease outcomes remain unproven/condition-specific.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Short-term trial safety appears generally acceptable, but long-term safety and efficacy remain uncertain.
Interaction data with anticoagulants/immunosuppressants/thyroid drugs are insufficient.
Regulatory status and product quality should be checked because marketplace status may change.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Long-term and interaction evidence remains limited; regulatory status and product quality should be re-checked because marketplace status may change.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Early human trials suggest NMN can affect NAD-related biomarkers, but clinical benefits remain preliminary and should be labeled uncertain.

records.typical_dose_range_en: ALA AI: ~1.1–1.6 g/day for adults. EPA+DHA supplement amounts vary; many products provide ~250–1,000 mg/day combined EPA+DHA, while prescription-level triglyceride treatment uses higher doses under medical supervision.

key_safety_notes.note_en: High-dose omega-3 can increase bleeding-time laboratory effects; clinically significant bleeding risk is usually low but anticoagulant/antiplatelet users need review, especially at high doses.
High-dose omega-3 may increase atrial fibrillation risk in some cardiovascular trials.
No characteristic thyroid-drug or immunosuppressant interaction.

anticoagulant.note_en: High-dose use warrants anticoagulant or antiplatelet review; clinically significant bleeding risk is usually low at common supplement doses.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: High-dose omega-3 may increase atrial fibrillation risk in some cardiovascular trials; fish-oil products are not interchangeable.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: EPA/DHA lower triglycerides at pharmacologic doses; cardiovascular outcome effects depend on formulation, dose, and population, so fish-oil products are not interchangeable.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No universal dose. Products commonly contain millions to tens of billions of CFU per serving; efficacy is strain-, indication-, and product-specific.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Usually few side effects in healthy people, but serious infections have occurred in vulnerable populations; FDA/NCCIH highlight particular concern in premature infants.
Use caution in severely immunocompromised or critically ill patients; this is the key immunosuppression-related safety flag.
Drug interaction data are not captured by a single class-wide rule.

immunosuppressant.note_en: Serious infections are rare but reported in severely immunocompromised or critically ill hosts; this is a host-risk flag, not a pharmacokinetic interaction.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: FDA and NCCIH highlight particular concern in premature infants; drug-interaction data are not captured by one class-wide rule across strains.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Some specific formulations show benefit for selected GI/other indications, but effects cannot be generalized across all probiotic strains/products.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA: 700–900 mcg RAE/day; adult UL for preformed vitamin A: 3,000 mcg RAE/day. Supplement content varies widely.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Chronic excess preformed vitamin A can cause toxicity.
Pregnancy: high-dose preformed vitamin A is teratogenic; avoid excess unless specifically medically indicated.
Retinoid medications can create additive toxicity concerns.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Retinoid medications create additive toxicity concerns, and high-dose preformed vitamin A is teratogenic in pregnancy.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Essential nutrient with established roles in vision, immunity, reproduction, and cellular differentiation; supplementation is primarily indicated when intake/status is inadequate.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA: 15 mg/day alpha-tocopherol. Supplements often provide much more; adult UL from supplements is 1,000 mg/day alpha-tocopherol.

key_safety_notes.note_en: High-dose vitamin E can increase bleeding tendency.
Use caution with anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy.
High-dose antioxidant supplementation can complicate some oncology treatment contexts; coordinate with oncology team.

anticoagulant.note_en: High-dose vitamin E can increase bleeding tendency; use caution with anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: High-dose antioxidant supplementation can complicate some oncology treatment contexts; coordinate with the oncology team.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Essential antioxidant nutrient; high-dose supplementation has not shown broad preventive benefit and can create safety concerns.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult AI: 90 mcg/day women and 120 mcg/day men. Supplement doses vary by K1/K2 form.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Major interaction with warfarin and related vitamin-K antagonist management; intake should be consistent and medically coordinated.
No established UL for natural K forms, but this does not remove drug-interaction risk.

anticoagulant.note_en: Major interaction with warfarin and related vitamin-K antagonists; intake should be kept consistent and medically coordinated.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: The absence of an established UL for natural K forms does not remove drug-interaction risk.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Essential for normal coagulation protein activation and bone-related proteins; its clinical importance is strongly tied to anticoagulant management.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA varies by age/sex; common iron-only supplements provide ~18–65 mg elemental iron. Adult UL is 45 mg/day from all sources, though therapeutic dosing can exceed this under medical supervision.

key_safety_notes.note_en: GI upset, constipation, nausea are common at higher doses.
Iron overdose is dangerous, especially in children.
Iron can impair levothyroxine absorption; separate dosing per thyroid-medication guidance.
Also interacts with several antibiotics and other medications.

thyroid.note_en: Iron impairs levothyroxine absorption; separate dosing per thyroid-medication guidance.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Also interacts with several antibiotics; iron overdose is dangerous, especially in children.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Strong evidence for treatment of iron deficiency; routine use without indication can cause harm or obscure the reason for abnormal iron status.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA: 55 mcg/day. Many supplements provide 50–200 mcg; selenium-only products may provide 100–400 mcg. Adult UL: 400 mcg/day.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Chronic excess can cause selenosis with hair/nail changes, GI symptoms, neurologic abnormalities and garlic-like breath odor.
No established role for high-dose selenium as a general cancer-prevention supplement.

thyroid.note_en: Selenoproteins participate in thyroid-hormone metabolism, but no blanket thyroid-drug interaction rule is established.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Chronic excess causes selenosis with hair and nail changes, GI and neurologic symptoms; more is not better.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Essential trace mineral in selenoproteins including antioxidant and thyroid-hormone metabolism pathways; more is not necessarily better.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Adult RDA: 150 mcg/day; pregnancy 220 mcg/day; lactation 290 mcg/day. Adult UL: 1,100 mcg/day.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Both deficiency and excess iodine can alter thyroid function.
High iodine intake can interact with thyroid disease management and thyroid-active drugs; clinician review is warranted.
Seaweed products can have highly variable iodine content.

thyroid.note_en: Both deficiency and excess iodine alter thyroid function and can interact with thyroid disease management and thyroid-active drugs.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Seaweed- and kelp-derived products can have highly variable iodine content.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Essential substrate for thyroid hormone synthesis; supplementation should respect baseline intake and thyroid context.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No RDA. Common adult supplemental doses range roughly 0.5–5 mg near bedtime; research uses wider ranges. Product labeling accuracy is variable.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Short-term use appears relatively safe; long-term safety is less established.
Drowsiness, headache, dizziness, nausea can occur.
Product-content variability is a known concern.
Use caution with sedatives and in children without clinical guidance.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Caution with sedatives and in children without clinical guidance; product-content variability against label is a documented concern.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: May help some circadian-timing disorders and jet lag; evidence does not support treating all chronic insomnia as a simple melatonin deficiency.

records.name_zh: 南非醉茄 / 印度人參
records.typical_dose_range_en: No standardized therapeutic dose. Many short-term trials use several hundred mg/day of standardized extract; formulations are not equivalent.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Rare liver injury has been reported.
Avoid in pregnancy; NCCIH advises against use in breastfeeding.
Not recommended before surgery or in autoimmune/thyroid disorders without clinical review.
Can interact with immunosuppressants, sedatives, anticonvulsants, diabetes/BP medicines, and thyroid hormone medications.

immunosuppressant.note_en: NCCIH lists interaction with immunosuppressants; autoimmune disorders warrant clinical review before use.

thyroid.note_en: Can interact with thyroid hormone medications; thyroid disorders warrant clinical review before use.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Also interacts with sedatives, anticonvulsants and diabetes or blood-pressure medicines; rare liver injury reported; avoid in pregnancy and not advised while breastfeeding.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Some preparations may help stress or insomnia, but studies are small and heterogeneous; benefits should not be generalized across products.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No universal standardized dose; studies use different species, plant parts, extracts, and dosing schedules.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Allergic reactions can occur and can be severe.
Theoretical interaction concern exists with immunosuppressants.
Possible liver-enzyme drug interactions are not fully resolved.

immunosuppressant.note_en: Theoretical interaction concern with immunosuppressants; not established in clinical data.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Allergic reactions can occur and can be severe; possible liver-enzyme drug interactions are not fully resolved.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: May slightly reduce the chance of catching a cold; evidence that it shortens an established cold is unclear.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No single standardized dose; study products vary substantially by preparation and sulfur-compound content.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Garlic supplements may increase bleeding risk.
Important perioperative and anticoagulant/antiplatelet review.
GI symptoms and odor are common; raw topical garlic can burn skin.

anticoagulant.note_en: Garlic supplements may increase bleeding risk; perioperative and anticoagulant or antiplatelet review is important.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: GI symptoms and odour are common; raw garlic applied to skin can cause burns.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: May modestly reduce LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, or glucose in some populations, but effects are small and product-dependent.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No universal supplement standard. Depression trials often use standardized extracts in divided daily dosing; product hypericin/hyperforin content matters.

key_safety_notes.note_en: High-priority interaction herb: induces drug-metabolizing pathways and can reduce effects of many critical medicines.
Can reduce warfarin, cyclosporine, oral contraceptive, HIV, oncology and other drug exposure.
Serotonergic combinations can cause serious serotonin-related toxicity.
Photosensitivity can occur.

anticoagulant.note_en: Induction of drug-metabolizing pathways can reduce warfarin exposure and destabilize anticoagulant control.

immunosuppressant.note_en: Can substantially reduce cyclosporine exposure, with transplant-rejection risk.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: High-priority interaction outlier: also lowers oral contraceptive, HIV and oncology drug exposure, and serotonergic combinations can cause serious serotonin-related toxicity. Warrants full medication reconciliation rather than a generic herb warning.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: May help some mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms, but interaction burden is unusually high and makes medication reconciliation essential.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Common osteoarthritis studies use ~1,500 mg/day glucosamine; formulations and pharmaceutical-grade products differ.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Evidence for knee osteoarthritis is inconsistent.
Warfarin interaction/INR elevation has been reported and should be reviewed.
Shellfish allergy concerns depend on product source/manufacturing rather than glucosamine molecule alone.

anticoagulant.note_en: Warfarin interaction with INR elevation has been reported at case level and should be reviewed.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Shellfish-allergy concern depends on product source and manufacturing rather than on the glucosamine molecule itself.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Substantial research exists, but guidelines disagree and results are inconsistent; product quality/formulation matters.

records.typical_dose_range_en: Common osteoarthritis studies use roughly 800–1,200 mg/day; pharmaceutical-grade preparations are not necessarily equivalent to retail products.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Evidence and guideline recommendations are inconsistent.
Potential anticoagulant interaction/bleeding concern warrants review, especially in combination products.

anticoagulant.note_en: Potential anticoagulant interaction or bleeding concern warrants review, especially in combination products.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Evidence and guideline recommendations are inconsistent; retail products are not necessarily equivalent to pharmaceutical-grade preparations.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: May help pain/function in selected osteoarthritis studies, but results vary and expert guidelines disagree.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No general RDA. Dietary-supplement studies often use ~600–1,200 mg/day, but indication-specific research varies.

key_safety_notes.note_en: GI effects can occur.
NAC is also used as a medication in specific clinical settings; supplement and medical-use contexts should not be conflated.
Drug-interaction evidence is indication-specific and incomplete.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: NAC is also used as a medication in specific clinical settings; supplement and medical-use contexts should not be conflated, and interaction evidence is indication-specific.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Biochemical precursor to glutathione with established medical uses as a drug; supplement evidence for general wellness is much less definitive.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No RDA or standardized therapeutic oral dose. Human supplement studies use varied doses and formulations.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Oral bioavailability and clinical outcomes vary by formulation.
Interaction data with anticoagulants, immunosuppressants, and thyroid drugs are insufficient.
Do not extrapolate intravenous or disease-specific research to routine oral supplement use.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Do not extrapolate intravenous or disease-specific research to routine oral supplement use; oral bioavailability varies by formulation.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Important endogenous antioxidant, but evidence that routine oral supplementation produces meaningful clinical outcomes remains formulation- and indication-dependent.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No universal safe/effective dose. Studies use varying catechin/EGCG amounts; concentrated extracts are not equivalent to brewed tea.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Rare liver injury has been reported, particularly with concentrated extracts.
High-dose green tea can reduce nadolol exposure; extract can alter atorvastatin exposure.
Caffeine-containing products add stimulant effects.
Medication interaction review is required.

anticoagulant.note_en: Anticoagulant relevance is product-dependent, turning on vitamin K content and caffeine context rather than one class rule.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: High-dose green tea can reduce nadolol exposure and extract can alter atorvastatin exposure; rare liver injury is reported with concentrated extracts.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: May modestly affect LDL cholesterol or body weight in some studies; evidence for cancer prevention is inconsistent.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No standardized therapeutic dose; clinical products vary widely in extract concentration and formulation.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Raw/unripe berries and some plant parts contain cyanogenic compounds and can cause GI toxicity; properly prepared products differ.
Medication-interaction data are limited.
Pregnancy/breastfeeding safety data are insufficient.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Raw or unripe berries and some plant parts contain cyanogenic compounds; pregnancy and breastfeeding safety data are insufficient.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Preliminary evidence suggests possible symptom relief in some upper respiratory infections, but evidence is limited and does not support broad antiviral claims.

records.typical_dose_range_en: No universal standardized dose; trials use varied extracts and ginsenoside content, often over weeks to a few months.

key_safety_notes.note_en: Insomnia is common.
May affect blood sugar and may interfere with blood clotting.
May worsen autoimmune disorders; medication interaction review is warranted.
Pregnancy safety is uncertain and some evidence raises concern.

anticoagulant.note_en: May interfere with blood clotting; anticoagulant or antiplatelet review is warranted.

immunosuppressant.note_en: May worsen autoimmune disorders; a host-context flag rather than an established drug interaction.

interaction_focus.focus_note_en: Insomnia is common and blood sugar may be affected; pregnancy safety is uncertain and some evidence raises concern.

records.evidence_snapshot_en: Human evidence is mixed; possible small effects on fatigue or selected metabolic/sexual outcomes, but many trials are small and short.
